88:1: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, Has there come to you, O Muhammad, the report of the Overwhelming Event? Meaning: its story and report. The commentators differed on the meaning of Al-Ghashiyah. Some of them said: It is the Resurrection that will overwhelm people with terrors. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Al-Ghashiyah is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. God has made it great and warned His servants about it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazd told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming Event? He said: The Overwhelming Event is the Hour. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming Event? He said: The Hour. Others said: Rather, Al-Ghashiyah means the fire that covers the faces of the infidels. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Sa’id, regarding his statement, Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming Event? He said: The Overwhelming Event of the Fire. The correct thing to say about this is that God said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming Event? He did not inform us that he meant the Overwhelming Event of the Resurrection, nor that he meant the Overwhelming Event of the Fire. Both are overwhelms. This one overwhelms people with affliction, terrors, and distress, and this one overwhelms the disbelievers with scorching faces, flames, and molten copper. There is no more correct statement about this than to say as He, may His praise be exalted, said, and the report of that is general as it is general.
88:2: And His statement: Some faces, that Day, will be humbled. God Almighty says: Some faces, that Day, which are the faces of the disbelievers in Him, will be humbled. He says: humiliated. It was mentioned by the one who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Some faces, that Day, will be humbled: meaning, submissive. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, humbled, he said: humbled in the Fire.
88:3: And his saying working means: working in the fire. settling means: settingtling in it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A working woman who is tired means she works and is tired in the Fire. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said: I heard Al-Hasan, he recited working and striving. He said: You did not work for God in this world, so work it in the Fire. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: A working, stubborn woman is someone who is too arrogant to obey God in this world, so He makes her work and makes her stubborn in the Fire. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, working and harassing, he said: working and harassing in the Fire. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, working and exhausting, he said: No one is more exhausted or more severe than the people of Hell.
88:4: And His statement: They will be burned in a blazing Fire. God Almighty says: These faces will be burned in a blazing Fire that has become very hot and intense. The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as tasalla with a fatha on the ta’, meaning: the faces are prayed over. Abu Amr read it as tasalla with a damma on the ta’, taking into consideration the statement: is given to drink from a vessel spring. The statement below is that they are two readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reciter reads, he is correct.
88:5: And his saying: They will be given to drink from a boiling spring, means: The people of these faces will be given to drink from a spring whose heat has reached its peak in the intense heat. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas: His statement, They will be given to drink from a spring that has been gushing for a long time. He said: It is one that has been gushing for a long time. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Atiyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, They are given to drink from a spring of water, he said: I have been cooking it since the day God created the world. Jacob told me again: Since the day God created the heavens and the earth. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, from a spring of water: It has reached its peak, and it is time to drink it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Its water is given to them from a spring of water means: It has been cooked since God created the heavens and the earth. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement, from a spring whose heat has reached its peak. He said: from a spring whose heat has reached its peak. Some of them said: What he meant by his saying from a present spring is two present springs. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, They will be given to drink from a spring of various kinds, he said: A spring of various kinds means present.
88:6: And His statement: They will have no food except from Dharee' means: Those who are the humble, hardworking, and weary ones on the Day of Resurrection will have no food except what they will be fed from Dharee'. Dharee' among the Arabs is a plant called shabraq. The people of Hijaz call dharee' when it dries up, while others call it shabraq, and it is poison. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention who said that. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They will have no food except from the thorny plant. He said: The thorny plant is the thorn bush. Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told me, he said: Ibad bin Ya’qub Al-Asadi told us, Muhammad said: Ibad told us, Muhammad bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman Al-Isfahani, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, They will have no food except from Dharee’, he said: The shabraq. Yaqub told me, he said: Ismail bin Aliyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said: Najdah, a man from Abd al-Qays, told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding His statement, They shall have no food except from Dharee’, he said: It is a thorny tree that grows low in the ground. When it is spring, the Quraysh call it Shabraq, and when the wood is strong, they call it Dharee’. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: They will have no food except from the thorny thorn. He said: The thorny thorn. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, Dhari’, he said: The dry thorn. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Except for the dharī’, he said: It is the shabraq when it dries and is called dharī’. Bishr told us: Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, They will have no food except from the thorny plant, meaning: from the worst, most hideous, and most abhorrent of foods. Mahmoud bin Ubaid told me, he said: Sharik bin Abdullah told us, regarding his statement: They will have no food except from Dhare’, he said: The shabraq. Others said: Adh-Dharee’ means stones. Mention who said that. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, regarding his statement, They will have no food except from the thorny plant, he said: stones. Others said: Adh-Dhari’ is a tree made of fire. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, They will have no food except from the thorny thorn, meaning: a tree of fire. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, They will have no food except from thorns of fire, he said: Thorns are thorns from fire. He said: As for this world, thorns are dry thorns that have no leaves, and the Arabs call them thorns of fire. In the Hereafter, they are thorns from fire.
88:7: And his saying: It neither fattens nor satisfies hunger means: This thorn will neither fatten nor satisfy hunger on the Day of Resurrection for those who eat it from the people of Hellfire, nor will it satisfy them from the hunger that befalls them.
88:8: God Almighty says: On that Day, faces will be soft, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection. They will be soft, meaning: they will be soft because God will give their people comfort in His Paradise, and they are the people of faith in God.
88:9: And His statement: She is pleased with her efforts, meaning: She is pleased with the work she did in this world in obedience to her Lord. It was also said: She is pleased with her efforts, meaning: She is pleased with the reward for her efforts in the Hereafter.
88:10: And his saying: In a high garden which is a garden. High means lofty.
88:11: And his saying: You will not hear therein any idle talk means: These faces will not hear the meaning for their people therein in the highest Paradise any idle talk, meaning by idle talk: a vain word. And idle talk: falsehood, so the word that is idle is called laghiya, just as the one who fixes the armor is called a shield, and the owner of the horse is called a knight, and the one who says the shughr is called a poet, and just as Al-Hutay'ah said: You stripped me naked and claimed that you are the son of a summer princess Meaning: Owner of milk and owner of dates. Some of the Kufians claimed that the meaning of this is: No false oath will be heard therein, and that is why it was called null and void. What he said has a doctrine and a reason, were it not that the people of interpretation from among the Companions and Followers were on a caliphate, and it is not permissible to take their disagreement on what they agreed upon. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention who said that. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, You will not hear therein any idle talk, meaning: You will not hear any harm or falsehood. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: You will not hear therein any idle talk, he said, cursing. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, You will not hear therein any idle talk, means you will not hear therein any falsehood or cursing. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, similarly. The reciters differed in the recitation of dhablak. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the reciters of Madinah, namely Abu Ja`far, recited it as la tasma` with a fatha on the ta`, meaning: do not hear the faces. Ibn Kathir, Nafi` and Abu `Amr recited it as la tasma` with a damma on the ta`, meaning that whose agent is not named. It is made feminine because of the feminization of laghiyah. Ibn Muhaysin also recited it with a damma, but he recited it with a ya`, as a masculine word. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that all of these are well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one reads, he is correct.
88:12: And his saying: There is a flowing spring in it, means: In the high Paradise there is a flowing spring that does not have a trench.
88:13: And his saying: In it are raised couches. “Couches” is the plural of bed, raised so that the believer may see, when he sits on them, all the bliss and kingdom that his Lord has granted him in it, and all of that will reach his sight. It was said: What he meant by his saying raised is: arranged. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: In it are raised couches meaning: arranged, like his saying: couches arranged, one on top of the other.
88:14: And his saying: And cups placed is the plural of cup, and they are the pitchers that have no spouts. We have already explained this, and mentioned what it contains in the narration, so there is no need to repeat it. What he meant by his saying placed is that they are placed on the edge of the running spring, so that whenever they want to drink, they find it full of drink.
88:15: And his statement: And cushions lined up means by cushions: pillows and cushions. And cushions: the singular is namariqah, with a damma on the noon. It has been narrated from some of Kalb, by hearing, namariqah, with a kasra on the noon and the ra. And it has been said: lined up because some of them are next to others. And the people of interpretation said in the text of what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, and cushions lined up means: the elbows. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And cushions lined up, meaning by cushions: the seating areas. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And cushions lined up, and cushions are pillows.
88:16: And His statement: And carpets spread out, God Almighty says: And in it are many carpets and rugs spread out, and the singular is: zarbiya, which is the rug that has a thin lining. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ahmad bin Mansour told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Sufyan, who said: Toba Al-Anbari told us, on the authority of Ikrimah bin Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ammar, who said: I saw Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, praying over Abqari, which is the carpet. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And carpets spread out: spread out.
88:17: God Almighty says to those who deny His power over what is described in this Surah, of the punishment and humiliation that He has prepared for those who oppose Him, and the bliss and honor that He has prepared for those who follow His rule: Do these deniers not look at the power of God over these matters, at the camels, how He created them, and made them subservient to them and made them carry their burdens while kneeling, then they rise with it? And He who created that is not unable to create what is described of these matters in Paradise and Hell. The Most High says: Do they not look at the camels, and take a lesson from them, and know that the power with which He was able to create them, will not make creating something similar to them impossible for Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: When God described what is in Paradise, the people of misguidance were amazed at that, so God revealed: Do they not look at the camels - how they are created? So camels were part of the Arabs’ livelihood and their property. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of someone who heard Shuraih say: Let us go out and see how camels were created.
88:18: And His saying: And to the heaven, how it was raised, God Almighty says: Do they not also look at the heaven, how He raised it, who informed you that He has prepared for His friends what He described, and for His enemies what He mentioned, so that they may know that His power is the power that nothing He wants to do is beyond His ability to do.
88:19: And His statement: And to the mountains, how they were erected, meaning: And to the mountains, how they were erected, not falling, so that they spread out on the earth. But by His power, We made them erect and solid, not moving from their place, nor shifting from their location. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, And to the mountains, how they are erected. The mountains rise up throughout the day, and when you reach the top, you reach gushing springs and hanging fruits, yet hands have not tilled it or worked it, a blessing from God, and the attainment of the appointed time.
88:20: And his saying: And to the earth, how it was spread out, meaning: And to the earth, how it was spread out. It is said: Dabal Mastah if it is flat at the top. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And to the earth, how it was spread out. That is, it was spread out. He says: Is not the One who created this able to create whatever He wills in Paradise?
88:21: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So remind O Muhammad, My servants of My signs, admonish them with My proofs, and convey My message to them. You are only a reminder He says: I only sent you to them as a reminder, to remind them of My blessings upon them, to make them aware of what is necessary for them, and to admonish them.
88:22: And his statement: You have no control over them means: You have no authority over them, nor are you a tyrant who can force them to do whatever you want. He says: They are all up to me, leave them and my judgment is over them. It is said: So-and-so has controlled his al-Nas 114:if he has authority over them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, You have no control over them, meaning: You are not a tyrant over them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: I have no control over them: meaning, all of My servants are in control. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Jahid, regarding his statement: in Musaytir, he said: a tyrant. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd, regarding His statement: “You are only a reminder. You are not a controller over them,” he said: You have no power over them to force them to believe. He said: Then after this came: Fight against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them (At-Tawbah 9:83) and He said: Little for them at every place of ambush (At-Tawbah 9:5) and watch them so that they do not go out into the land. “But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah, then let them go on their way. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful” (At-Tawbah 9:5). He said: So You are not a controller over them was abrogated. He said: He came to kill him or he becomes Muslim. He said: And the reminder is as it is, it was not abrogated. And he recited: And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers (Adh-Dhariyat 51:55). Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, ‘There is no god but God.’ When they say, ‘There is no god but God,’ their blood and their wealth are safe from me, except for a right due, and their reckoning is with God.” Then he recited: “You are only a reminder. You are not a controller over them.” Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: Abu al-Zubayr said: Then he recited: “You are only a reminder. You are not a controller over them.” Yusuf bin Musa Al-Qattan told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the same.
88:23: And his statement: Except for he who turns away and disbelieves is directed at two aspects: So mention your people, O Muhammad, except for he who turns away from you and turns away from the signs of God and disbelieves. So his statement except is an exception from those who were reminded, even if they were not mentioned, as one says: So-and-so passed away and called except for he whose response is not expected, meaning: So he called the people except for he whose response is not expected. The second aspect: To make his statement: Except for he who turns away and disbelieves disconnected from what precedes it, so the meaning of the statement then is: You have no control over them, except for he who turns away and disbelieves, God will punish him. Similarly, the disconnected exception is tested by making if good with it. So if it is good with it, then it is disconnected, and if it is not good, then it is a connected exception, like the saying of the one who says: The people marched except Zayd. And entering if is not appropriate here because it is a correct exception.
88:24: And his saying: Then God will punish him with the greatest punishment is the punishment of Hell. He says: Then God will punish him with the greatest punishment for his disbelief in this world, and the punishment of Hell in the Hereafter.
88:25: And His saying: Indeed, to Us is their return, means: Indeed, to Us is the return and resurrection of those who disbelieved.
88:26: Then it is up to Us to bring them to account. He says: Then it is up to God to bring them to account, and He will recompense them for their past disobedience to His Lord. This informs His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, that He is the One who will punish them, not him. He is the One who will reward and punish, and that He is the One to whom the reminder and the conveyance of the message will be directed. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Except for he who turns away and disbelieves, he said: His reckoning is with God. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: “Indeed, to Us is their return. Then upon Us is their account.” He says: Indeed, to God is the return, and upon Him is the account.
